transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

My mind keeps getting stuck on the same upsetting thoughts about messing things up for my family and at work, and I can’t let them go. It’s started to feel like I'm constantly trapped in my own head, and I just don't know how to make it stop.
Do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts, like checking or counting, to reduce the distress from these thoughts?

Yes, I feel incredibly driven to do that. To calm myself down, I end up rereading emails, medical notes, and server configs three or four times, and silently running through mental checklists. I just can't move on to the next thing until it feels "just right," even though I know it's wasting my time.
Do these repetitive thoughts or behaviors take up at least one hour per day or significantly interfere with your work, relationships, or daily activities?

Yes, they easily take up hours of my day and have seriously disrupted my life. I waste so much time rechecking everything that I miss important details at work, and I've had to pull back from community events and mentoring because I'm just too mentally exhausted and worried about making a mistake.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F42", "F32", "F41.1"], but based on this conversation, F32 (depressive episode) and F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder) are less likely because the patient's primary symptoms revolve around intrusive, distressing thoughts related to making mistakes, along with compulsive behaviors (re-reading, mental checklists) performed to reduce anxiety, which are hallmark features of F42 (obsessive-compulsive disorder). The compulsions are time-consuming (several hours daily) and significantly impair functioning, meeting diagnostic criteria for F42. There is no clear evidence of pervasive low mood or excessive worry across multiple domains typical of F32 or F41.1. Therefore, the current candidate is narrowed to F42.
